title: Grateful Dead Live at Stanley Theatre on 1972-09-28
lineage: Primary Source: SBD> MR> DAT> CDR> WAV> SHN

ai_review.summary: High‑energy ’72 show with a monster Other One and killer China→Rider, captured on a mostly soundboard matrix that sounds excellent once the rough audience intro clears.
ai_review.review: The concert is praised for its blistering second set – especially the soaring Other One, the epic Playin', and an unforgettable China > Rider stretch – and the band’s tight playing throughout. The recording is a mixed‑source (matrix) tape: early audience cuts are noisy and Loser loses vocals, but the soundboard portions are crisp and often described as “A‑” or five‑star quality. Overall fans rate both the performance and the audio very highly.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (8 out of 10) award 4‑5 stars, highlighting outstanding musical moments and generally excellent sound quality despite a few early audience glitches.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early AUD segments are muddy and Loser lacks ~5 min of vocals; mix can be Bob‑Weir heavy in places. Once the SBD (soundboard) kicks in, clarity is high, with crisp balance and no major dropouts.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set solid with fun cuts (Half‑Step, Tennessee Jed, Promised Land) and a strong China/Rider finish; second set builds into an extended jam marathon highlighted by Other One, Bobby McGee and a seamless return to the finale.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly called "off the charts"; his Strat is described as mean, triumphant, and golden on the Other One and other jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for tight, powerful bass work (the “Phil zone” from El Paso to Wharf Rat) and overall solid foundation.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for strong early‑70s guitar tone, though some mention a too‑prominent mix; vocal on El Paso highlighted as excellent.
